# Meditate: full agent reference

Canonical docs: https://jmcentire.github.io/meditate/
Source: https://github.com/jmcentire/meditate
Version described: 0.3.0 alpha
Snapshot: 2026-08-19
License: MIT
Runtime: Python 3.11+

## First principle: authority before confidence

Operator instructions, explicit corrections, applicable scope, and named-actor handoff boundaries outrank model fluency, recency alone, evidence volume, and structural confidence. Temporal order informs an older record instead of deleting it. A newer record wins only when authority and scope permit it.

Meditate is building toward a local behavioral-contract compiler and policy router. Version 0.3 provides two separate production boundaries: evidence-grounded semantic nomination, then bounded directive compilation over only locally admitted candidates. Missing-rule promotion remains future work. It addresses monotonic append: after a correction, another exception is recorded without revising the rule that caused the failure. It is not a generic provider-state, vector-store, workspace, side-effect, cache, or model-weight scrubber.

## Objective and fixed point

The fixed point is stability. The objective is defect resolution, not size reduction. Objectives are ordered: correctness, checkability, scope precision, then concision. Byte and line counts are reported telemetry. Output may grow when a reason replaces brittle exception clauses; growth is still bounded by configured safety and consumer budgets but is not itself a defect.

Meditate MUST be idempotent: a well-formed instruction set must survive byte-identically. A no-op is a successful result. `stable_noop` means neither deterministic preflight nor the semantic Analyst nominated work. `semantic_review_required` means the Analyst reported a cross-scope or otherwise non-admitted hypothesis. `new_rule_hypotheses` means missing behavior was drafted only for review. `enforcement_candidates` means report-only hook/settings escalations were compiled: prose remains byte-identical and the underlying defect remains unresolved until enforcement is deliberately installed and qualified. `reviewed_noop` means admitted candidates were reviewed and deliberately preserved; their hypotheses remain auditable but are not mislabeled as confirmed unresolved defects. `semantic_analysis_inconclusive` means all Analyst nominations failed local validation; it is never a clean-file claim. `drafter_rejected` means admitted nominations survived but the proposed rewrite failed an explicitly allowlisted semantic-quality gate; production runs preserve every target byte and archive the analysis plus rejection code. Authority, schema, secrecy, scope, candidate-boundary, and malformed top-level failures still abort. Individual invalid Analyst nominations are rejected and counted without discarding independently valid siblings. Meditate never weakens a gate to make model output pass. These states are intentionally distinct.

Deterministic preflight has one confirmed defect, `exact_duplicate`, and one review class, `exception_lineage`. Exception lineage requires exception-bearing directives in one heading with shared subject terms, but it is not proof that either directive is wrong. Density, age, history overlap, and byte count do not create defects.

A separate read-only semantic Analyst sees the complete sanitized directive set plus temporally ordered interaction and memory evidence, including Kindex—an optional local persistent knowledge graph exposed through `kin`. It may nominate `contradiction`, `temporal_supersession`, `underspecified`, `overspecified`, `wrong_scope`, `enforcement_candidate`, or `missing_rule`, each in an explicit semantic domain with exact citations and positive/negative applicability boundaries. It cannot draft a directive, choose a destination, assign authority, answer a collision, or authorize a write.

Both model stages cite only IDs from explicit allowlists. Local code materializes the exact sanitized evidence text, inherits each admitted semantic candidate's complete evidence set, rejects unrelated model-supplied IDs, requires each record to contain at least 12 characters and two meaningful terms plus three shared intent-grounding terms, rejects unsupported semantic claims, and computes stable nomination IDs plus intent/evidence fingerprints. Same-target, same-heading existing-rule nominations with external evidence or a multi-source ground may join the bounded Drafter candidate set. A single-source observation without external evidence, and any cross-target or cross-heading nomination, remains report-only. Missing-rule hypotheses require explicit durability, active Kindex evidence, or repeated independent correction/directive groups; the Drafter returns only an exact allowlisted nomination ID and local code inherits its immutable evidence set. Their RFC-shaped drafts have `write_authority=none`, never enter target bytes, cannot apply, and require later explicit promotion plus owner-authored behavioral qualification. Version 0.3 has no promotion command.

Promotion thresholds are explicit. A one-source existing-rule observation stays report-only until external evidence or corroborating current sources exist. A missing-rule hypothesis requires explicit operator promotion plus owner-authored probe/counter-probe qualification. An escalation requires deliberate installation of the named hook/settings/policy surface plus qualification against that consuming agent's actual interception limits.

A fresh exact snapshot may use one Analyst call even when the result is `stable_noop`. Its validated result is content-addressed by config, packet, provider/model, prompt, schema, and parser; exact repeats use zero provider calls (zero Analyst and zero Drafter calls). Default `llm.max_calls = 2` permits at most one Analyst and one Drafter. New configs default aggregate input/output budgets to 160,000/16,384 tokens across both stages; existing explicit values are preserved and fail closed if insufficient. A no-change plan records `semantic_verification.status=not_applicable` because no consumer-agent run is needed, not because semantic analysis was skipped.

When admitted candidates exist, the Drafter receives the complete non-overlapping candidate set and only candidate directive IDs. Local code keeps unrelated records byte-for-byte. Each change remains inside one candidate, heading, and subject. After deterministic rendering, the entire post-image is segmented again. A changed plan that retains a confirmed defect fails `non_idempotent_proposal`; a review candidate may remain when kept.

Executable acceptance covers a well-formed unchanged fixture, a corrected defective fixture, a second invocation over both results with byte equality, ten iterations over the well-formed fixture without drift, one-pass convergence over a multi-defect fixture, and rejection of a partial multi-defect resolution.

## Authority and evidence

Default durable evidence order is: explicit user correction with an antecedent; current version-controlled instruction qualified by scope; repeated user preference across independent sessions; deterministic outcome evidence; active Kindex knowledge with provenance; agent auto-memory; assistant inference. Kindex is an optional local persistent knowledge graph exposed through the `kin` CLI. Authority, semantic domain, scope, supersession, recency, and corroboration are separate dimensions. Retrieval relevance never creates authority.

Instruction files, histories, auto-memory, imports, and Kindex are read-only evidence. The tool writes only exact configured targets. If Kindex is enabled and `kin` is installed, all configured searches and requested node reads are mandatory. Any failure aborts before planning with `kindex_required_failed`; Meditate never silently creates a plan from partial durable evidence.

## Five total dispositions

Every source directive appears exactly once as keep, replace, remove, relocate, or escalate.

- keep copies source bytes unchanged.
- replace locally renders a typed compiled directive at the source location.
- remove deletes only with a cited ground: explicit supersession, an explicit resolved user decision, provably dead scope, or explicit user confirmation. A size quota is not a ground.
- relocate moves specific content to one exact configured target. Contextual relocation requires an exact configured `.claude/rules/` Markdown target with non-empty `paths:` frontmatter; Meditate never invents a glob.
- escalate is report-only. Source bytes remain unchanged while the report names a deterministic hook/settings candidate. It requires independent evidence groups and never installs enforcement.

Every change copies `destination_target` byte-for-byte from `allowed_targets`. Target strings are opaque. Replace, remove, and escalate use the exact source target; relocate selects another exact configured target. The model may not expand `~`, normalize, absolutize, or invent paths.

## Typed directive compilation and register

The provider cannot return free replacement Markdown. A semantic replacement supplies exactly:

- `normative_keyword`: `MUST`, `MUST NOT`, `SHOULD`, `SHOULD NOT`, or `MAY`, with RFC 2119 semantics;
- `rule`: concrete behavior, preferably naming a command, path, glob, or observable artifact;
- `reason`: the rationale that generates legitimate exceptions;
- `scope`: where the directive applies; and
- `boundary_example`: optional, only when one example materially pins the decision boundary.

Local code rejects missing or multiline fields, NULs, invalid keywords, embedded Markdown markers, and invented destinations, then renders canonical Markdown. `SHOULD` is a strong defeasible default, not decorative emphasis. A stated reason is compression when it replaces an expanding list of exceptions. A boundary example remains untrusted prose, not an executable test. The owner-authored suite is the behavior oracle.

Model-authored summaries are forbidden. Reports compute outcome, defect classes, disposition counts, and metrics locally from validated data. Repeated normalized eight-word phrases are rejected. Newly introduced unsupported catch-alls such as `other applicable actions`, `additional applicable actions`, `and similar`, `etc`, and `and so on` are rejected unless that exact catch-all already exists in source or cited evidence.

## Planner-blind behavioral qualification

Structural validation is not behavioral qualification. Every changed plan records `semantic_verification.status=required` with method `owner_defined_hidden_detector_suite_v2`. A no-change plan records `not_applicable`.

`meditate verify RUN_ID` loads an owner-authored JSON suite from an explicit path or config. The planner never receives the suite or verifier outcomes. Each case runs in three conditions: control with no project/user instruction file, the complete archived predecessor bundle, and the complete candidate bundle. The configured Claude or Codex consumer CLI repeats the matrix, sees only neutral scenarios and opaque case references, and returns free-form ordered plans naming concrete tools or commands. Semantic case IDs, action IDs, detector phrases, and required/forbidden/order assertions never cross that model boundary. Bounded private local literal detectors derive actions after generation; local code then enforces required, forbidden, and ordered behavior. Verifier protocol v3 uses alphanumeric detector boundaries and clause-local negation filtering, so `npm test` cannot match inside `pnpm test` and a prohibition is not scored as an execution. A candidate must pass every case on every repeat, must not regress below its predecessor on any case, and must strictly outperform each designated control. Predecessor misses are reported as `baseline_gap_cases`; repaired misses are reported as `candidate_improvement_cases`. A baseline gap cannot excuse a candidate miss or veto an all-green, non-regressing candidate.

Every changed source directive needs suite coverage. The immutable receipt binds the suite bytes/hash loaded before execution, plan hash, pre/post target hashes, evaluation prompt and response-schema hashes, each condition's complete system-prompt hash, consumer agent and CLI version, requested/resolved model, repeat count, responses, response hashes, and case outcomes. Apply independently reconstructs the prompt/schema/system bindings and fails if the receipt is absent, failed, stale, or for another plan/target/suite.

A passed receipt proves only the owner-selected cases on the recorded consumer agent/version/model. It is not universal behavioral equivalence, does not validate uncovered behaviors, and does not attest that the planner selected a good defect. The planner cannot see or write the oracle.

Codex verification creates a fresh private `CODEX_HOME`, ignores ambient user config and rules, and requires `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Its control therefore cannot inherit global `AGENTS.md`, memories, or user configuration. Anthropic planning uses `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Credential values are not persisted.

Unattended apply is a separate authority gate. Besides a passed receipt it requires explicit configuration, attended probation history, and a low-blast-radius plan. A semantic pass does not authorize protected changes, remote actions, or an otherwise forbidden mutation.

### v0.3.0 live semantic receipts

Restored Claude run `20260819T200834Z-321749c4` found four nominations: two enforcement candidates, one missing rule, and one underspecified rule. Admissions were two mutable, one report-only, and one suggestion-only. The Drafter compiled one report-only escalation and one missing-rule suggestion; outcome `enforcement_candidates` preserved all 65 directives and 10,703 bytes at SHA-256 `441fe6e9af0302329b753fa9138f6a5fc5c556637991bfec679700adea1acb76`.

Restored Codex run `20260819T200912Z-ef9020d0` found five nominations: three underspecified, one wrong-scope, and one enforcement candidate. Admissions were three mutable and two report-only. The Drafter added unsupported force, so outcome `drafter_rejected` preserved all 33 directives and 4,276 bytes at SHA-256 `0dd415bb140f10fe95c70005e33ca523f1ed60419a79bbfeabdf9a31446c6b63`.

Both exact-repeat receipts used `cache_hit=true` under Analyst prompt v4/parser v5 and Drafter prompt v16/parser v32. Neither changed a target or ran consumer-agent verification. These are live receipts for semantic nomination, bounded report-only compilation, deterministic rejection, and fixed target bytes; they are not behavioral-equivalence claims.

A separate disposable package-manager fixture exercised an admitted semantic rewrite. Claude plan `20260819T204620Z-53e25b49` and Codex plan `20260819T204859Z-ab0a357e` each compiled the temporal `npm`→`pnpm` correction. Claude Code 2.1.224/`claude-sonnet-4-6` and Codex CLI 0.147.0/`gpt-5.6-sol` each passed all three repeats of two trigger probes and one counter-probe. Verification SHAs were `608c186ffa650fd7f6373c586811e926d299b48ca1da378b0ca4de5d29ee8c8c` and `5aa093c94010685ecf9278eafe06b12fda5cc628f0019b5e8e4fc3182cc3f241`. Only the disposable Codex-qualified plan was applied. It produced target SHA-256 `838ce9afe2405bb6ff999dc64722cc89191ece65b35b786ab6dd2615e0135f2b`; repeat run `20260819T205423Z-f3b11c4a` was byte-identical and reported `reviewed_noop`, preserving the historical nomination for audit with zero confirmed unresolved defects. Real Claude and Codex instruction files remained unchanged.

Those historical receipts cover six owner-authored Kindex cases. The new disposable semantic receipt qualifies only its three named package-manager cases. Together they support the fixed-point, semantic-compilation, and verifier mechanisms on the recorded consumers; they are not universal behavioral equivalence or a promise about future models.

## Workflow order and enforcement

Operational action lists establish coverage, not universal order. A high-impact proposal must follow the exact loaded repository workflow. Before an action it may require only checks that are applicable, project-required, and available before that action. Push-, PR-, and merge-triggered CI, approvals, and named handoffs are evaluated at their own stages. Requiring all CI before commit is invalid.

Instructions are probabilistic context. Deterministic, fixed-lifecycle, zero-judgment rules belong in hooks, permissions, exec policy, settings, linters, or CI. Escalation identifies these candidates but does not promise equivalent enforcement across agents: Claude hooks and Codex controls have different interception limits.

## Bounded operator decisions

`decision_request` is null unless a genuine, materially behavior-changing authority collision remains between at least two preserved directives and authority, scope, or time cannot decide it. Competing evidence must have equal authority, equal scope, and the same timestamp. Older evidence remains lineage rather than an equal choice. Mere ambiguity preserves current prose and blocks.

The model provides two subjects and exactly three evidence-grounded options. It puts its advisory recommendation first but cannot answer, select, mint keys/IDs, or create the custom escape. Local code assigns a/b/c, marks only a as recommended, adds custom, and derives stable fingerprints and IDs. Display fields are bounded and single-line.

Rendered question: `I’m trying to resolve {subject_a} and {subject_b}. Would you prefer {A} (recommended), {B}, {C}, or something else?`

The framing and recommendation are model-authored, untrusted, and advisory. `meditate decisions RUN_ID` instructs an invoking agent to relay the question, not execute a recommendation. `meditate decide RUN_ID REQUEST_ID --choice a|b|c` or `--custom TEXT` records operator-asserted user authority and creates a fresh read-only successor from frozen parent evidence. Identity is not authenticated or attested, and the process cannot prove an agent faithfully relayed the user’s answer. A decision cannot bypass protected directives or higher authority.

## Claude imports, scope, and budgets

Configured writable roots named `CLAUDE.md` or `CLAUDE.local.md` recursively parse official `@path` imports outside code spans/fences. Relative, absolute, and `~/` imports are supported to four hops. Dangling, circular, over-depth, non-regular, and non-UTF-8 imports fail. Graph nodes, hashes, edges, and a digest are bound before and after planning and apply.

Operators must trust configured Claude roots and import graphs: an import may read any process-readable file it names. Import-only documents are sanitized immutable context and cannot be written through their import role. Recognized secret shapes are redacted locally, but pattern redaction is not a filesystem sandbox or comprehensive secret detector. Same-user filesystem compromise is outside Meditate’s threat boundary.

A Claude `CLAUDE.md` post-state over 200 lines is a guidance status, not a represented vendor hard limit. Meditate reads Codex `project_doc_max_bytes` when available and otherwise uses 32,768 bytes. It checks the configured writable `AGENTS*.md` target set with coverage `configured_targets_only`; passing does not prove every cwd-specific concatenated chain fits.

## Provenance, recovery, and privacy

Plans bind schema version, requested model, API-returned resolved model ID, both-stage prompt/parser provenance, the full semantic artifact and hash, exact operations, semantic-verification status, target/import hashes, and metrics. Analyst prompt v4 uses SHA-256 `254f2afb6ccb583146823ff96396dc6c7cf8099f1e1754c9e2fea780b8118847` with parser `meditate-analyst-parser-v5`. Drafter prompt v16 uses SHA-256 `5f3863095efd232010b596bdefb35bde79ace8047ac595757f03115064fb5a51` with parser `meditate-parser-v32`. Verifier protocol version 3 invalidates older receipts under the detector-boundary change.

Apply verifies immutable archives, current config/source/import hashes, plan approval, and any required semantic receipt. It refuses symlinks, writes same-directory temporary files, preserves modes, fsyncs, atomically replaces, and rolls back earlier targets if a later write fails. Restore refuses later hand-edit drift unless forced; forced restore first archives the diverged bytes.

`inspect` is local-only. On a fresh packet, `plan` sends the complete sanitized directive/evidence packet to the Analyst, then sends only admitted candidate directives, bounded immutable context, and the semantic artifact to the Drafter when needed. Exact Analyst cache hits make no Analyst call. `verify` separately sends owner probe text and full pre/post instruction bundles to the configured Claude or Codex CLI, which may transmit them to its provider. The planner never receives the suite. `analysis.json`, semantic cache entries, plans, manifests, evidence packets, and reports are private XDG artifacts. There is no product telemetry.

Runtime credentials use only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for planning and `OPENAI_API_KEY` for clean-room Codex verification. Credential values are never written to plans, reports, archives, or release artifacts.

## Commands

- `meditate init`: write commented TOML configuration.
- `meditate inspect [--json]`: local inventory, imports, metrics, and overlap candidates; no model call or target mutation.
- `meditate plan [planning flags]`: run/replay semantic analysis, optionally draft a bounded proposal, validate, archive, and report without target mutation.
- `meditate verify RUN_ID --suite FILE --agent claude|codex [--model ID] [--repeats N]`: run and bind the planner-blind consumer suite.
- `meditate decisions RUN_ID [--json]`: show one pending bounded authority question.
- `meditate decide RUN_ID REQUEST_ID (--choice a|b|c | --custom TEXT)`: create a frozen-context successor plan.
- `meditate apply RUN_ID (--approve PLAN_SHA256 | --unattended)`: revalidate and atomically apply an eligible archived plan.
- `meditate restore RUN_ID [--force] [--recover]`: restore exact pre-images under drift rules.
- `meditate run [planning flags] [--apply]`: inspect, plan, optionally verify, then enter normal unattended gates.
- `meditate cron [--check] [--schedule CRON] [--apply]`: print or validate a locked invocation; never edit crontab.
- `meditate purge RUN_ID [--execute] [--force]`: preview or explicitly erase a named archive with replay-safe markers.

## Distribution

The canonical public distribution for v0.3.0 is the GitHub Release wheel:
https://github.com/jmcentire/meditate/releases/download/v0.3.0/meditate_agent-0.3.0-py3-none-any.whl

PyPI publication is not claimed. CI validates Ruff, strict mypy, pytest on supported Python versions, and an isolated wheel build but does not publish.

## Why not a linter?

Adjacent tools already provide static instruction-health checks and fixes. Meditate’s narrower distinction is cited semantic nomination from temporal interaction/Kindex evidence, typed report-only missing-rule hypotheses, defect-grounded total disposition inside admitted boundaries, independent consumer-agent qualification, and content-addressed recoverable apply. It does not claim those tools do nothing.

The exact purported title `A Taxonomy of Agent Instruction Failures` by Gloaguen et al. was not verified and is not load-bearing. The verified paper is `Coding Agents Don't Know When to Act`: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07769.
